title: Catherine O’Hara Honored By Macaulay Culkin, Annie Murphy and Dan Levy During Emotional Emmys In Memoriam: ‘She Was Our Mama’
description: Catherine O’Hara, who died in January at 71, was honored Monday night at the 78th Emmy Awards by her three former on-screen children Macaulay Culkin
body:
Catherine O’Hara, who died in January at 71, was honored Monday night at the 78th Emmy Awards by her three former on-screen children Macaulay Culkin, Annie Murphy and Dan Levy.

	Culkin opened the tribute, describing his “Home Alone” mom as “encouraging,” “warm” and, of course, “funny.” 

	“She wasn’t just a wife and mother to Bo and Matthew and Luke. She was my mom. She was our mama,” he said. “And by extension, she’s all of our mama. By the way, call your mother tonight. Give it up for moms. But like a good mama, she always showed up when I asked her to. Because that was Catherine. That’s what she did. She showed up. And this is the best that we can do for her tonight.”
	

	Murphy then took the mic. She played O’Hara’s daughter, Alexis, in “Schitt’s Creek.” Murphy described O’Hara’s laugh as a “perpetual ‘yes’,” adding that it “challenged anyone who heard it to join in and be as delighted as she was.” She went on to recall all the affection she received from strangers after O’Hara died. 


	“After we lost Catherine, I was passed a note on an Air Canada flight that said, ‘She was so special. I hope you’re doing okay,'” Murphy recalled. “On a drive up north, I was hugged by an extremely gruff-looking gas station attendant who was also grieving her loss. While buying wine at the LCBO, I was treated to a very lively Catherine mashup, which was a woman saying, ‘Ew, David, where’s the baby?’ while doing what I can only assume was Catherine’s exquisite hobble from ‘Best in Show.’ These are only a very few of the interactions I’ve been lucky enough to have that remind me how profoundly Catherine has impacted the world.”
	

	Levy, who played O’Hara’s son David on “Schitt’s Creek,” went last. He said that the “greatest lesson” her learned from O’Hara was “to always say yes” to everything “both professionally and personally.”

	“Say yes to her naming that wig,” Levy said. “Say yes to giving her space to experiment and create. It will amaze you on a daily basis, and it will change your life. Say yes to her dinner invites and her stories and her wisdom and her generosity. Those are the things you will hold onto the tightest. Always say yes to any opportunity to revel in the presence of greatness.”

	O’Hara’s death was announced by her agency, CAA. She died in her Los Angeles home following a brief illness.

	Her five-decade career in Hollywood began on the Canadian sketch comedy series “Second City Television.” The show, which she co-created with her future “Schitt’s Creek” co-star Eugene Levy, earned her an Emmy in 1982. She went on to star in films like O’Hara went on to star in films such as “After Hours,” “Beetlejuice” and the first two “Home Alone” movies.

	O’Hara also starred in several of Christopher Guest’s mockumentaries, including “Best in Show,” “For Your Consideration,” “Waiting for Guffman” and “A Mighty Wind.”

title: Zendaya and Tom Holland Make Emmys Debut After Wedding
description: Tom Holland is swinging through the Emmys for the first time ever to join Zendaya, his wife and co-star on “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “The Odys
body:
Tom Holland is swinging through the Emmys for the first time ever to join Zendaya, his wife and co-star on “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “The Odyssey.” 

	While “SNL” star Marcello Hernández was introducing the best director for a comedy award, he did a bit about all the stars he was most excited to see. Among them was Zendaya. As the camera cut to “The Drama” star, we could see her husband, Holland, smiling wide behind her. 


	“I want to say hi to Zendaya,” Hernández said. “Hi. You’re a beast and you’re amazing. And I saw you and I wanted to play it cool, and I’ve decided I can’t do that. So, I would like to invite you and Spider-Man to have dinner at my house.”
	

	Zendaya is celebrating her sixth and final Emmy nomination for “Euphoria.” She is nominated for outstanding lead actress in a drama series, which she has won twice before for her role as Rue.

	The couple stepped out in couture. Zendaya also wore Les Pétales Place Vendôme White South Sea Cultured Pearl earrings, while Holland was in Dior.

	“I loved the idea of taking something as timeless as Mikimoto pearls and making them feel fresh, modern and young,” Zendaya’s longtime stylist Law Roach said in a statement. “There’s an elegance to pearls that will always be classic, but the way Zendaya wears them tonight feels completely of the moment.”

	Roach on the red carpet retracted previous claims that Holland and Zendaya got married in private earlier this spring. 

	“I actually lied; she wasn’t married. They actually haven’t had an official ceremony yet; it’s gonna happen after the ‘Dune’ press tour,” Roach said.
	

	When pressed, Roach confirmed no wedding has happened, and any social media content of the wedding is false.

	“She’s been his wife for a really long time now, but it’s not official yet,” he said.

	This year has been a momentous one for the couple. Along with their alleged private nuptials earlier this spring, the two co-starred in “The Odyssey” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” two of the year’s biggest blockbusters. With $923 million to date in North America, “Brand New Day” is primed to soon overtake 2015’s “Star Wars: The Force Awakens” ($936 million, not adjusted for inflation) as the highest-grossing movie of all time at the domestic box office.

	After such a busy year, Zendaya told Fandango in March that she will “go into hiding for a little bit.”

	“I guess, you know, I just hope people don’t get sick of me,” she said. “And I really appreciate everyone who supports any of the movies or supports my career in any kind of way. I’m deeply appreciative, and like I said, I just hope you guys don’t get sick of me this year.”

schema.headline: Zendaya and Tom Holland Make Emmys Debut After Wedding

title: Michael J. Fox Earns Huge Emmys Ovation and Inspires Tears as He Accepts Humanitarian Award: ‘Accepting Parkinson’s Didn’t Mean I Had to Surrender to It’
description: Michael J. Fox‘s heartfelt speech at the Emmys earned a huge ovation as he accepted the Bob Hope Humanitarian Award on Monday night. The five-time E
body:
Michael J. Fox‘s heartfelt speech at the Emmys earned a huge ovation as he accepted the Bob Hope Humanitarian Award on Monday night. The five-time Emmy winner was recognized for his “transformative contributions to Parkinson’s disease research and advocacy.”

	Fox said during his speech, which was intro-ed by his “The Good Wife” co-star Julianna Margulies, “Thank you to everyone involved with the Television Academy for this amazing, humbling honor.”
	

	He spoke about the award’s namesake, Bob Hope, and the entertainer’s tireless dedication to helping people. “I learned from his example. I couldn’t have known how these lessons would resonate in my own life, until my late 20s, when my life handed me a role I wasn’t looking for. Initially I kept my Parkinson’s diagnosis a secret. I worried it would affect my work and relationships with audiences. Would they laugh if they knew I was sick? I was stunned by the support from all of you, so uplifted and I hadn’t lost what I do. They couldn’t take it away from me. And it’s because you stood up for me. … I understood that accepting Parkinson’s didn’t mean I had to surrender to it. It just meant I had to do everything I could for everyone living with this disease.”


	“I set out to advocate for Parkinson’s disease and raise money,” he continued. “I found people to lead the effort for me and vowed to fund the best science in the world. I’m proud of the progress we’ve made to benefit Parkinson’s patients and families. We move closer to eradicating this disease forever. I’m deeply grateful to our staff, donors, researchers, and most of all the patient community who make our work at the Michael J. Fox foundation possible.”
	

	Fox went on to thank his wife, the rest of his family and Bob Hope, for “showing me how it’s done.”

	Fox was also nominated for guest actor in a comedy series for an appearance on “Shrinking,” though Rob Reiner ended up winning the trophy posthumously. 

	The “Family Ties” star launched the Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson’s Research in 2000 after disclosing his diagnosis of Parkinson’s in 1991 at the age of 29. 

	Oprah Winfrey was the first to win the Bob Hope Humanitarian Award, which was first given in 2002. The award was created “to honor a member of the telecommunications industry whose philanthropic efforts exemplify Bob Hope’s own decades-long altruism and positive impact on society.” Last year’s Bob Hope honor went to Ted Danson and Mary Steenburgen. 

	The honoree is selected by the Television Academy and the Bob & Dolores Hope Foundation to find a person whose “humanitarian efforts have brought credit to the industry and whose deeds and actions have had a lasting impact on society.”

schema.headline: Michael J. Fox Earns Huge Emmys Ovation and Inspires Tears as He Accepts Humanitarian Award: ‘Accepting Parkinson’s Didn’t Mean I Had to Surrender to It’

title: Dolly Parton Gets Emotional Emmys Tribute as Reba Sings ‘Appalachian Memories’ and Sally Field Declares: ‘God Bless You, My Friend’
description: The Emmy Awards paid tribute to Dolly Parton with a performance by Reba McEntire, who performed the late artist’s song “Appalachian Memories.” The 1
body:
The Emmy Awards paid tribute to Dolly Parton with a performance by Reba McEntire, who performed the late artist’s song “Appalachian Memories.” The 1983 country song was written and recorded by Parton for her twenty-fifth solo studio album, “Burlap & Satin.”

	Sally Field, who starred with Parton in the 1989 film “Steel Magnolias,” introduced the tribute. (Field was also on hand at this year’s Emmys because she’s nominated, in the lead actress in a limited/anthology series or movie category, for Netflix’s “Remarkably Bright Creatures.”)
	

	“Over the years, I never stopped loving her though we lived very far apart,” Field said. “I adored her from day one. How could you not?”


	“She was genuine and humble, supportive and blisteringly funny with a bawdy sense of humor that would send any rude guy looking for a place to hide,” she continued. “I couldn’t see then what a real giant Dolly was — not just as an artist, but as a human. She was a humanitarian whose contributions have made a profound difference in the lives of so many in her home state of Tennessee and across our country.”

	“God bless you Dolly Parton, my friend,” she concluded. “I am not the only one on Earth that will love you forever and ever.”

	McEntire then took the stage for an orchestral performance of “Appalachian Memories,” which Parton performed at the 1983 Emmys ceremony. A clip from that broadcast played before McEntire’s version, with Parton saying “I grew up in the smoky mountains, the Appalachian Mountains. I have written a song that touches me very deep. I’m sure in your own way, you will  to this. This song, like I say, is very important to me. And I hope you don’t like it. If you don’t like it, if you don’t mind, I would rather not hear about it later.”
	

	The country music icon died in Nashville on Aug. 25 at 80 years old following a brief battle with cancer. Her sister, Stella, recently revealed Parton hid her diagnosis from fans and several family members to ensure their final memories of her weren’t filled with sadness. 

	“Dolly did not want anybody to tell that because Dolly could not bear negative things,” Stella said on “CBS Mornings.” “She would not have wanted her fans worried about it… She didn’t want a lot of the family worried about it.”

	Parton publicly hinted at health struggles but never revealed the extent. A week prior to her death, Parton appeared in a video to promote a new roller coaster at her Dollywood theme park after canceling an in-person appearance due to dizziness and dehydration. She also canceled her Las Vegas residency last year due to “health challenges,” later canceling the rescheduled dates as well.

	In 2022, Parton was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame and subsequently released her final album, “Rockstar,” one year later. She was also inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame, Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame and Songwriters Hall of Fame. Parton later became a National Medal of Arts honoree and a Kennedy Center Honors recipient. 

	“Jolene” and “I Will Always Love You” are among Parton’s most famed songs, solidifying her status as a country music icon. Parton received 11 Grammys throughout her career and starred in films such as “9 to 5,” “The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas” and “Steel Magnolias.”

	Parton founded The Imagination Library in 1995, which gives free books to children under 5 years old. Last year, the charity announced it had gifted over 300 million books since its creation.

title: Rob Reiner Remembered as ‘Our Beloved Meathead’ and ‘Cherished Legend’ by Teary Jamie Lee Curtis in Emmys’ In Memoriam
description: Rob Reiner received a heartfelt tribute during Monday’s Emmy Awards, with folk singer Noah Kahan leading a strings-backed rendition of Simon & Garfu
body:
Rob Reiner received a heartfelt tribute during Monday’s Emmy Awards, with folk singer Noah Kahan leading a strings-backed rendition of Simon & Garfunkel’s “Bridge Over Troubled Water” during the In Memoriam section as actress Jamie Lee Curtis invoked Reiner’s “All in the Family” character to commemorate his life.

	“Last year we lost another cherished legend, our beloved ‘Meathead,’ Rob Reiner,” a teary Curtis told the audience as she closed out the In Memoriam section. “He was generous and kind and funny as hell and a friend to all.”
	

	He also received a posthumous Emmy win in the guest actor in a comedy series category for “The Bear” on the second night of the Creative Arts Awards.


	Reiner took home his first Emmy win for best supporting actor in 1974 for his role as Michael “Meathead” Stivic in “All in the Family,” and he won again in 1978. Forty-eight years later, the comedic icon’s legacy lives on, adding a third Emmy win to his name and breaking the record for longest span between acting Emmy wins — a record his father, fellow comedian Carl Reiner, previously held. 

	Reiner died in December 2025 at age 78. He has been remembered across the industry as the legendary filmmaker behind classics like “This Is Spinal Tap,” “The Princess Bride,” “When Harry Met Sally” and “A Few Good Men.” His guest appearance on FX’s “The Bear” was one of his final on-screen performances.

	Reiner and his wife Michele were allegedly stabbed to death in their home in Brentwood by their son Nick Reiner. He is currently in holding at the Twin Towers Correctional Facility after a Los Angeles County grand jury indicted him on two counts of first-degree murder with special circumstances of “lying in wait” and “multiple murders.” These circumstances make him eligible for the death penalty. He will appear before a court on Oct. 23 for a hearing to access $1.5 million in trust assets so that he can rehire his private defense attorney. 
	

	“We all miss Robbie, Michele and all those we lost this year,” Curtis said.

	The couple’s death sent shock waves of sadness through the industry. Reiner received a heartfelt tribute at the 2026 Oscars during the In Memoriam section led by his friend and collaborator Billy Crystal. 

	“My friend Rob’s movies will last for lifetimes because they were about what makes us laugh and cry and what we aspire to be: Far better in his eyes, far kinder, far funnier and far more human,” Crystal said. “To the millions who have enjoyed his films all these years, I want you to know here and around the world, how many times Rob told me that it meant everything to him that his work meant something to you. And for us who had the privilege of working with and knowing him and loving him, all we can say is, buddy, what fun we had storming the castle.”

	He was also honored at the 2026 Critics Choice Awards. Host Chelsea Handler finished her opening monologue by sharing heartfelt words about the late director.

	“Everyone in this room knows that the nicest guy in Hollywood was Rob Reiner,” Handler said. “Rob and Michele were tireless in their efforts to so many important causes, all stemming from one basic idea: decency and that we should all look out for each other. I think we can all agree that we definitely need more of that. So let’s use tonight as a reminder of that decency and as a reminder of everything Rob and Michele represented and fought so hard for.”

schema.headline: Rob Reiner Remembered as ‘Our Beloved Meathead’ and ‘Cherished Legend’ by Teary Jamie Lee Curtis in Emmys’ In Memoriam

title: Matthew Rhys Makes Emmy History as First Person to Win Two Lead Acting Emmys in One Night and First Man to Win All Three Top Acting Prizes
description:
Matthew Rhys did something no actor had done in 78 years of the Emmy Awards.

	Rhys won two lead acting Emmys on the same night at Monday’s ceremony
body:
Matthew Rhys did something no actor had done in 78 years of the Emmy Awards.

	Rhys won two lead acting Emmys on the same night at Monday’s ceremony. Earlier in the night he shockingly took home the lead actor (limited) for his work in Netflix’s “The Beast in Me.” Later on, he nabbed the lead comedy actor prize for Apple TV’s “Widow’s Bay.” 

	He’s now the first person ever to claim both lead actor prizes in a single ceremony, and adding to his 2018 drama win for “The Americans,” the pair of statuettes also makes him the first male performer to win in all three lead acting categories.
	

	Two performers had won two acting Emmys on one night before, but neither did it in the lead categories: James Earl Jones swept lead drama actor for “Gabriel’s Fire” and supporting actor (limited) for “Heat Wave” in 1991, and Stockard Channing took two supporting actress trophies in 2002, for “The West Wing” and “The Matthew Shepard Story.” Rhys is the first to do it at the top of two ballots at once.

	Rhys, already a previous Emmy winner for lead drama actor in 2018 for “The Americans” and now, “Widow’s Bay” and “The Beast in Me” hands him the complete set of lead acting Emmys across drama, comedy and limited, a trifecta no actor had ever assembled. Three men have been close: Robert Young and Carroll O’Connor each won the drama and comedy leads, and Andre Braugher took drama and limited. The only performer of any gender to complete the set before Rhys is Barbara Stanwyck, who won all three lead actress categories between 1961 and 1983 — though the earliest of hers predates the split between the comedy and drama races. (Among the actresses still stuck one short is Claire Danes, Rhys’ “Beast in Me” co-star.)
	

	In the limited race he pulled off the bigger surprise, edging the presumptive favorite Oscar Isaac (“Beef”) along with Riz Ahmed (“Bait”), Jason Bateman (“Black Rabbit”) and Charlie Hunnam (“Monster: The Ed Gein Story”). On the comedy side, Rhys topped Yahya Abdul-Mateen II (“Wonder Man”), Steve Carell (“Rooster”), Jason Segel (“Shrinking”) and Martin Short (“Only Murders in the Building”). 

	The Welsh actor also has two additional nominations as an executive producer on both of his series. 

	This year’s Emmy nominations were led by “The Pitt” with 25 nominations, followed by “Hacks,” “Widow’s Bay” and “Beef.”

schema.headline: Matthew Rhys Makes Emmy History as First Person to Win Two Lead Acting Emmys in One Night and First Man to Win All Three Top Acting Prizes

title: Hiro Murai Becomes First Asian Director to Win Emmy for Comedy Directing With ‘Widow’s Bay’
description:
Hiro Murai has made Emmy history.

	Murai on Monday won outstanding directing for a comedy series for the “Widow’s Bay” premiere, “Welcome to Widow’
body:
Hiro Murai has made Emmy history.

	Murai on Monday won outstanding directing for a comedy series for the “Widow’s Bay” premiere, “Welcome to Widow’s Bay!,” becoming the first Asian director ever to win the category — and only the third Asian director to win in any Emmy category.

	He prevailed over a deep field that included Randall Einhorn (“Abbott Elementary”), Christopher Storer (“The Bear”), Andrew DeYoung (“The Chair Company”), Lucia Aniello (“Hacks”) and Mary Lou Belli (“The Ms. Pat Show”).
	

	The other Asians directors who have won previously include Lee Sung Jin for the first season of the anthology series “Beef” and Hwang Dong-hyuk for the first season of the drama series “Squid Game.”


	The Japanese filmmaker, who holds 11 career Emmy nominations, had twice been recognized in comedy directing — for “Atlanta” and “Mr. & Mrs. Smith.” He was already a previous Emmy winner as an executive producer on the first season of “The Bear.” The “Widow’s Bay” win, for the pilot that set the show’s tone, anchors the craft dominance that carried the series to a leading field for a freshman show.

	This year’s Emmy nominations were led by “The Pitt” with 25 nominations, followed by “Hacks,” “Widow’s Bay” and “Beef.” Matthew Rhys scored a nomination for lead actor for “Widow’s Bay,” along with supporting stars Dale Dickey, Kate O’Flynn and Stephen Root. Creator and showrunner Katie Dippold also recevied a nom for outstanding writing for a comedy series for the pilot.

	“Katie Dippold, thank you for being brilliant and letting me ride shotgun,” Murai said on stage. “I’m so proud of everything we did. And most of all, I just want to thank my family and my partner Emma. I love you. Thank you.”

schema.headline: Hiro Murai Becomes First Asian Director to Win Emmy for Comedy Directing With ‘Widow’s Bay’

title: Sally Field Becomes Oldest Emmy Winner in Her Category and Shades Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger: ‘Our Voices Matter’
description: Sally Field won the Emmy for lead actress in a limited or anthology series or TV movie on Sunday, recognizing her portrayal of Tova Sullivan in the
body:
Sally Field won the Emmy for lead actress in a limited or anthology series or TV movie on Sunday, recognizing her portrayal of Tova Sullivan in the Netflix film “Remarkably Bright Creatures.” At 79, she is the oldest actress to win in this category, edging out Jessica Tandy (“Foxfire” in 1987) by months.

	This is Field’s 10th Emmy nomination and fourth win. She previously took home the gold for her roles in “Sybil” (1977), “ER” (2001) and “Brothers & Sisters” (2007).
	

	Field was shocked as she took the stage to accept her trophy, and squealed before beginning her speech. “This was not supposed to supposed to happen! OK, I gotta talk really, really quick.” But once she got going, she was fired up. “I have been so grateful and so proud to be a part of this community — the arts — for 62 years or something,” she continued. “With art, we matter. Our voices matter. Our diversity, our unique story telling matters.” Seemingly referencing the pending merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, she added, “We can’t let those voices be silenced or compromised or merged.”


	Along with “Sybil,” “ER” and “Brothers & Sisters,” Field’s best-known credits include playing the title role in “Norma Rae” (1979) and Edna Spalding in “Places in the Heart” (1984), which both earned her Academy Awards, and Mary Todd Lincoln in “Lincoln” (2012), which earned her an Academy Award nomination.

	Also nominated for this year’s lead limited series or TV movie actress Emmy were Carey Mulligan (“Beef”), Sarah Pidgeon (“Remarkably Bright Creatures”), Claire Danes (“The Beast in Me”) and Sarah Snook (“All Her Fault”).

schema.headline: Sally Field Becomes Oldest Emmy Winner in Her Category and Shades Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger: ‘Our Voices Matter’

title: Stephen Colbert Wins Emmy After ‘Late Show’ Canceled by CBS and Tells Industry to Hire His Crew: ‘They Will Make Your Show Better!’
description: “The Late Show With Stephen Colbert” is the sole Emmy winner of this year’s outstanding variety series category, via the canceled CBS late-night ser
body:
“The Late Show With Stephen Colbert” is the sole Emmy winner of this year’s outstanding variety series category, via the canceled CBS late-night series’ final season, which ended in May. 

	“I want to thank so many people in this room,” he said. “Over the last 21 years, I’ve interviewed at least a thousand of you. Thank you for coming on to talk to this idiot, I want you to know that you were the perfect guest. The segment went great, and I’m sorry I forgot to play your clip. But of course, there can only be one favorite guest, and that is my wife, Evie McGee. Thank you, darling.
	

	“I want to say to the audience thank you so much for watching. watching. We hope you enjoyed the show. We had a great time doing it for you. That’s it. Thank you. We’ll catch you all on the flip.”


	Colbert noted that his writing team (which won the show’s first Emmy for variety series writing last weekend) were tasked with writing Monday night’s Emmy jokes. 

	“The thing about these late shows is that, besides bringing a really good, steady job, is that they require so many people that they’re a fantastic incubator for young people to come in to learn to work professionally on a deadline in cooperation in collaboration, and that is the future of our business that we have to look after. I want you to know I got some great news: They are all tech avail. Hire them; they will make your show better, and they will make your day easier.”

	“The Late Show” beat out “The Daily Show” (Comedy Central), “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” (ABC), “Last Week Tonight with John Oliver” (HBO Max), “The Late Show with Stephen Colbert” (CBS) and “Saturday Night Live” (NBC) in the newly remerged variety series competition, which brought together the previously separated outstanding talk series and outstanding scripted variety categories.
	

	As part of this rule change, the Academy decreed that the outstanding variety series category would now be an “area” award. Nominees in “area” award categories aren’t actually competing against each other — they’re all independently trying to get at least 90% of Emmy voters to say “yes” when asked, “Does this nominee merit an Emmy?” Any nominated show will win an Emmy if 90% of voters agree.

	That means the category could have had as many as five winners. And the Emmy producers were ready for that possibility. What if multiple, or all, of the variety series nominees had won? “Local news is going to be late,” exec producer Jesse Collins said during Thursday’s Emmys press day. “That’s what’s going to happen. If multiple people win, each would get up to give their speech and it’ll be a TV moment.”

	But 90% is a high threshold, which is why the TV Academy decided that if no series surpassed a 90% “yes” vote, the show with the highest “yes” vote would be the sole winner. And ultimately, that may have been the case, as “The Late Show” was the only winner.

	During the first weekend of the Emmys, “The Late Show” already won four prizes: Outstanding Writing For A Variety Series, Outstanding Directing For A Variety Series, Outstanding Technical Direction and Camerawork For A Series, Outstanding Lighting Design/Lighting Direction For A Series and Outstanding Picture Editing For Variety Programming (Segment).

	“The Late Show” has won nine Emmys over the course of its run; last year it landed the kudos for outstanding talk series and directing for a variety series. Those were the show’s first two wins — which now means that all of “The Late Show With Stephen Colbert” Emmy victories came after CBS announced that it had canceled the show (despite its status at the time as the No. 1 talker in late night).

schema.headline: Stephen Colbert Wins Emmy After ‘Late Show’ Canceled by CBS and Tells Industry to Hire His Crew: ‘They Will Make Your Show Better!’

title: Emmy Executive Arrivals: Top TV Leaders Keep Their Cool on an Indigo Carpet
description:
Sep 14, 2026 6:59pm PT	
	

	
		Emmy Executive Arrivals: Top TV Leaders Keep Their Cool on an Indigo Carpet
body:
Sep 14, 2026 6:59pm PT	
	

	
		Emmy Executive Arrivals: Top TV Leaders Keep Their Cool on an Indigo Carpet
	
	
			


			
			
	

									Chad Salvador
	

		
	
				

	The heat wave that has blanketed Los Angeles for more than a week broke Monday afternoon just in time for TV movers and shakers to gather on an indigo-colored carpet outside the Peacock Theater in downtown Los Angeles for the 78th annual Emmy Awards.

	The assembly of top leaders this time included some fresh faces, including newly appointed Apple CEO John Ternus and Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro. Ternus told Variety he was enjoying his first major award show, especially with Apple TV so well positioned with a big haul of nominations for “Widow’s Bay,” “Shrinking,” “Pluribus” and more.” 

	“I might be the world’s biggest Apple TV fan,” Ternus said, assuring that he is a big consumer of TV and film. “I love the shows, I love the movies and the work that we’ve done, and it’s only been seven years. There’s so much good content. There’s so many great stories, and we’re just going to keep building on that.”

body:
Meg Stalter
                          I'm Manifesting an Emmy!!!
                      
      
    
            They say dress for the part you want and Meg Stalter's taking it literally ... dressing like an Emmys trophy as she hit the awards show red carpet.
      
    
            Meg pulled out all the stops ... covering herself head to toe in gold paint and donning a massive pair of gilded wings.
      
    
            The comedy queen is nominated for her first Emmy tonight ... she's up for Outstanding Supporting Actress In A Comedy Series for her role as Kayla Schaeffer in "Hacks."
      
    
            The HBO series is one of the most-nominated shows this year, earning a whopping 24 nods ... trailing "The Pitt" by just one.

title: Cheerleader Mother-Daughter Murder-Suicide: Weed Gummies, Prescription Bottles Found at Scene
description:
Cheerleader Mother-Daughter Murder-Suicide
                          Weed Gummies, Prescription B
body:
Cheerleader Mother-Daughter Murder-Suicide
                          Weed Gummies, Prescription Bottles
                          Scattered Around Death Scene
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                September 14, 2026
                
                            4:18 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 14, 2026
                                5:49 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Tawnia McGeehan, who allegedly killed her daughter Addi Smith in a murder-suicide while in Vegas for a cheer competition, had several medications in her system at the time she took her and her daughter’s lives, TMZ has learned. 
      
    
            TMZ obtained the Clark County Medical Examiner report for Tawnia and Addi’s deaths. The document listed the causes of their deaths as gunshot wounds to the head.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The report said Tawnia’s ex-husband called cops for a welfare check after failing to get ahold of the two in February 2026. 
      

            Staff at the Rio Hotel went to the room to find a note outside the room warning, “Call 911 before walking in. Two dead bodies and one is an 11-year-old.”
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The hotel staff found Tawnia and Addi in a bed. The cops arrived and found two suicide notes inside the room … one that said Addi had been “heavily medicated” beforehand. 
      
    
            The officers found multiple prescription bottles in the room for Tawnia and an open package of THC cannabis gummies and bottles of over-the-counter sleep aids. They also found what appeared to be broken and mostly empty gabapentin capsules and a clear cup containing white residue near the trash can. 
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Per the report, officers found cartridge casings on the floor and a Ruger handgun. The report said Tawnia tested positive for medicines that are used for depression, insomnia, and anxiety.
      
    
            The report said Tawnia had a history of severe depression with previously prescribed depression medication. “They were aware of past suicidal ideation but denied knowledge of past attempts,” the filing said. An officer noted Tawnia had “reportedly been severely depressed over breakups and an ongoing custody battle with her ex-husband.

title: Hayden Panettiere's L.A. Neighbors Saw 'Shady' Alleged Drug Dealer One Week Before Death
description:
Hayden Panettiere
                          L.A. Neighbors Saw 'Shady' People Dropping Off Bags
body:
Hayden Panettiere
                          L.A. Neighbors Saw 'Shady' People Dropping Off Bags
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                September 14, 2026
                
                            3:14 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 14, 2026
                                5:58 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Hayden Panettiere's neighbors were suspicious of three "shady" people who regularly came to the actress' West Hollywood condo for years … and believed they were drug dealers, TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Sources who live in Hayden's building tell TMZ ... they saw two women and a man coming to her unit "frequently" from 2021 until the week before Hayden's death.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            One neighbor said the last time they saw the man -- a week before Hayden's death -- he came with a bag with the name "Brian" on it. We're told the man looked to be in his mid-30s, while the two women appeared to be in their early 20s.
      

            We're told the 3 people never showed up together ... each arrived alone. One source tells TMZ they would see little bags being delivered to Hayden's unit ... the actress would open the door, take the bags, and that was it. "They never stayed, they'd just leave," said the source, who added they have not seen the people since Hayden's death. 
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Sources close to Brian tell TMZ they often ordered from Postmates. That would not explain, however, the same 3 people showing up for years.
      
    
            As TMZ first reported, sources connected to the death investigation believe Hayden took a fatal pill the day she died … purchased from her "long-time drug dealer" in L.A., who sold her oxycodone. Our sources believe Hayden consumed a pill that was laced with fentanyl. 
      
    
      
      One fatal pill ended Hayden Panettiere’s life.Now, we’re learning more about the deadly drug—and who authorities are investigating in connection with her death. pic.twitter.com/wr1oF7orC3
              @TMZ
  
    
            We're told the DEA is actively looking at the dealer.
      
    
            Hayden's toxicology results are pending, and results could take several more weeks.

title: Late Migos Rapper Takeoff's Alleged Murderer Wants to Examine Bullets From Fatal Shooting
description:
Late Migos Rapper Takeoff
                          Alleged Murderer Wants To Examine Bullets
body:
Late Migos Rapper Takeoff
                          Alleged Murderer Wants To Examine Bullets
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Late Migos rapper Takeoff's alleged murderer, Patrick Xavier Clark, is making moves to examine evidence, including the supposed bullets from his fatal shooting ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            According to court docs, obtained by TMZ, Clark wants permission to review certain items in the Houston Police Department's possession.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Patrick said he wants an independent expert to examine the evidence to help build his defense ahead of trial, which is scheduled for November. 
      

            As TMZ first reported, Clark was arrested for allegedly shooting the former Migos member in the head at a bowling alley in Houston.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Takeoff, whose real name was Kirsnik Khari Ball, died in 2022 ... and Clark denied he was involved in the shooting. 
      
    
            In addition to the upcoming murder trial, Takeoff's parents are involved in a bitter battle over how much each parent gets from a civil lawsuit settlement.
